stemMd: How many real solutions does $4^x-5(2^x)+4=0$ have?
explanationMd: Set t=2 to the power x, so t>0. The quadratic (t−1)(t−4)=0 gives t=1 or 4, corresponding to x=0 or 2. There are two real solutions.

distractorRationale.b: This omits one positive substituted root.
distractorRationale.d: A quadratic in a one-to-one exponential has at most two such roots.
distractorRationale.a: Both roots after substitution are positive and admissible.
distractorRationale.e: This treats exponential inversion like taking square roots.
